providers.pricingNotes: Pro, iad1: active CPU $0.128 per vCPU-hour of CPU time (I/O wait not billed), memory $0.0212 per GB-hour of wall time in one-minute minimum increments, $0.60 per million creations. Vercel's docs leave rounding after the first minute open; we charge whole minutes, the dearer reading. Metered: the bench stops each sandbox to read Vercel's meter before deleting it, so the meter includes the stop's disk snapshot (about 3% in one probe; approximate, not corrected per task). Hourly assumes every vCPU busy. Pro's $20 credit, data transfer and snapshot storage excluded.

providers.pricingNotes: Sandbox rates ($0.1419 per CPU-hour, $0.024 per GiB-hour; one Modal CPU is a physical core). Billed per second on max(request, usage), minimum request 0.125 CPU. Priced on the requested allocation, never on the guest's MemTotal, which shows the host's memory without a size. A sized sandbox pins request = limit, so its estimate is exact. The default track (0.125 CPU, 128 MiB request) bursts into spare host capacity and that usage is billed too, so its estimate is a lower bound. A pinned region adds 1.15x (broad, such as us) or 1.75x (narrow, such as us-east). No disk charge or creation fee listed; plan credits excluded.

Published Sandboxes runtime rates ($0.0655/vCPU-hour, $0.0211/GB RAM-hour), priced on the allocation. Billing increment and minimum not stated; one-second estimate. Free promotional period excluded. Realistic build runs mount an 8 GiB volume (fix-and-test mounts none), priced at $0.16/GB-month for the sandbox's lifetime. Snapshots and stored images not used.

Published usage rates: $0.004/vCPU-hour and $0.00225/GiB-hour of memory, per second while running (not while starting, paused or stopped). Paid plans include disk (Builder 1 TiB across machines), beyond that $0.08/GiB-month; each machine's 20 GiB /data is counted as included. Plan fee and monthly credits ($20 Pro, $100 Builder) and egress ($0.02/GiB beyond the plan's) excluded. Default agent-browser template is 4 vCPU / 8 GiB.

Published Sandboxes rates on the Performance tier, the default ($0.05/vCPU-hour, $0.01/GiB RAM-hour), priced on the allocation and billed per millisecond while running (2026-11-18). Shared ($0.011, $0.0055) and Spot ($0.0063, $0.00135) tiers are cheaper and not used. Disk not billed. The snapshot tests did not run: Beam has no API to delete a memory snapshot. Credits excluded.

Published Sandboxes rates on the Shared tier ($0.011/vCPU-hour, $0.0055/GiB RAM-hour; shared vCPUs, not preemptible, up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB), priced on the allocation and billed per millisecond while running (2026-11-20). Run with the adapter's cpuTier option. Disk not billed. Credits excluded.

Published Sandboxes rates on the Spot tier ($0.0063/vCPU-hour, $0.00135/GiB RAM-hour; spare capacity, reclaimed with 30 seconds' notice), priced on the allocation and billed per millisecond while running (2026-11-20). Run with the adapter's cpuTier option. Disk not billed. Credits excluded.

sourceNotes.pause-resume: Pause and resume are from the previous run (Oct 22, SDK a2316c3): the provider's own API, which the SDK update does not touch. Superserve's is from this run, at 4 vCPU. boxd's is from its Nov 19 re-run in New York. Vercel's is from its Nov 9 run (SBX-103). Baseten's is from its own pause runs (Nov 17), timed from its first command after standby. Instabox's is from its own runs (Nov 18). Maritime's is from its own runs (Nov 24). Styne's is from its own runs (Nov 23).
sourceNotes.burst-10: E2B's bursts of 10 are from a rerun on Nov 18 on the same SDK commit (1185278), after one of its first three bursts had two creates time out on E2B's side. The rerun ran only bursts of 10, so they came closer together than in the first run, which alternated them with bursts of 25. As with every run we stopped early, the first run's failures aren't counted. Maritime's bursts of 10 are from a rerun on Nov 24 on the same SDK commit (619307b), each burst started a minute apart to stay inside Maritime's create rate (30 a minute per API key). Its first bursts ran back to back, and Maritime refused the creates past that rate with HTTP 429; that run is replaced and its failures aren't counted, among them one create whose first command found Maritime's service unreachable.
sourceNotes.burst-25: Maritime's bursts of 25 are from a rerun on Nov 24 on the same SDK commit (619307b), each burst started a minute apart to stay inside Maritime's create rate (30 a minute per API key). Its first bursts ran back to back, and Maritime refused the creates past that rate with HTTP 429; that run is replaced and its failures aren't counted, among them one create whose first command found Maritime's service unreachable.
sourceNotes.cold: Maritime's main tests are from a rerun on Nov 24 on the same SDK commit (619307b), started 70 s after its bursts on the default machine. Its first run began two seconds after them, and Maritime refused its first 27 creates with HTTP 429 (30 creates a minute per API key); that run is replaced and its failures aren't counted, among them 3 creates whose first command found Maritime's service unreachable and one pause with no response.
